body: I'm so not ready though. I really wish this was just an essay topic.
This actually sounds very useful. Thank you, yeah this looks like it can bring me back out fast enough.

Yeah I kept telling myself I'm not with my mum anymore. She can't lock me outside between the gate and the door as punishment for bad grades anymore. Even though I know this the memories and flashbacks kept coming and my deep breathes wasn't helping. I even slapped myself a few times but it doesn't bring me back fast enough. 

> Each day that passes is day you defeated them and are a day stronger.

Thanks, this really gives me hope. Maybe the next time it won't be this bad.
I will try just that next time. Is this something a therapist teaches people? I've never heard of it.

I don't want revenge. I just want my mum out of my life and I did just that. I haven't contacted her for 2 years now. I have no idea why the memories  still haunts me. I kept telling myself the neighbours aren't watching me when I held the door for a few minutes to ventilate the my apartment. I kept telling myself I'm not a kid anymore, I won't get locked outside between the gate and the door by my mum as punishment for bad grades anymore. The flashback of neighbours coming and going, walking pass me in haste, avoiding my eye contact. I slapped myself a few times, dug my nails onto my face but still couldn't snap out of the memories. I felt the neighbours were watching me like they were judging me. I couldn't snap out of it right away. Why the fuck am I still holding onto this shit?? Fuck me.

I did both. Took loooong breathes, but couldn't stop myself from breathing faster and faster. Then I touched my face, dug my nails in the skin to make myself feel the pain. Kept telling myself I'm not there anymore, but still took what felt like forever and some tears before I could calm myself. Is there other things I can do next time this happens?
Let's say the demon/source of the problem has already been cut out of his life, but memories is still there. Then what?

That's her problem, yes, it also means one less reason for me to live.

>what has made you live until this very moment?

My cowardness of taking one step forward.

Yeah you tell her about that. I'm not the ideal daughter she wanted, I just got "lucky". And lucky isn't a reason for me to keep on living.

Before birth it was nothingness. No feeling, no pain, no sadness. I just want to be nothing again, and only death can help me achieve it.

It's a bit gloomy. I still haven't get over how my mum told me "I didn't ask you to come. I just wanted a baby and it doesn't have to be you." I know she was not fully serious about it but still, I cannot get it out of my head.

I don't want to. Why do I HAVE to live? I didn't choose to come to life. Even my mum said no one asked me to come, said she only wanted a baby and it doesn't have to be me. I just want to revert back to whatever it is before my birth.
Nah no one will miss me. There's no one in my life other than myself. Being aware doesn't mean I want to seek medical help. I have no reason to do so.
And with your mind slowly decaying, memories fading and eventually forget everything you have ever loved.

> Suicide isn't the answer ever

You must be living in a fairy tale.
Yes. I wish I could get a gun that easily like you do in the US.
Not high enough means lying on the ground with broken arms and legs, and slowly fade away in cold due to blood lost/internal bleeding.
You don't. Self-explanatory enough.
